'''Christopher J. Cramer''' (born September 23, 1961) is a research [[chemist]] and served as vice president for research at the [[University of Minnesota]] from 2018–2021.<ref name=HigherEd2018>{{cite news |date=2018-10-19 |title= Transitions: Naval Postgraduate School Selects New President, New Provost Named at Cabrini U. |url= https://www.chronicle.com/article/Transitions-Naval/244848 |work=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]] |access-date=2020-09-01 }}</ref> He presently serves as executive vice president and [[chief research officer]] for [[UL (safety organization)|Underwriters Laboratories Inc.]]<ref name=APNewswire2021>{{cite news |date=2021-03-08 |title= Underwriters Laboratories Names Dr. Christopher J. Cramer as Chief Research Officer |url= https://apnews.com/press-release/pr-newswire/business-science-executive-changes-chemistry-math-and-science-education-252aa41fdc5a8cb8071310e0a4e6cccb |work=[[AP News]] |access-date=2021-06-02 }}</ref>

==Education==
Cramer studied [[mathematics]] and [[chemistry]] at [[Washington University in St. Louis]], Missouri. He earned a Ph.D. in chemistry from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]],<ref name="Insight2018">{{cite news |last=Coss |first=Kevin |date=2018-11-13 |title=Meet Christopher J. Cramer, New Vice President for Research |work=Inquiry: Exploring the Impact of University Research |location=[[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]] }}</ref> working with doctoral advisor [[Scott E. Denmark]].<ref name=RealScientists2015>{{cite web |url= http://realscientists.org/2015/05/10/artisinal-organic-chemistry-chris-cramer-joins-real-scientists/ |title=Artisanal Organic Chemistry: Chris Cramer Joins Real Scientists |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2015-05-10 |website=Real Scientists |access-date=2020-09-09}}</ref>

==Military service==
Cramer served for four years as an officer in the [[U.S. Army]] [[Chemical Corps]] from 1988 to 1992, including combat duty in [[Iraq]] during [[Operation Desert Storm]].<ref name="Bachrach2014">{{cite book|author=Steven M. Bachrach|title=Computational Organic Chemistry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKsEAwAAQBAJ&pg=PT870|date=3 March 2014|publisher=Wiley|isbn=978-1-118-67122-1|pages=870–}}</ref>

==Scientific career==
In 1992, Cramer joined the faculty in the University of Minnesota's department of chemistry, where he remained for his entire academic career. In addition to teaching and research, Cramer was director of both undergraduate and graduate studies in the chemistry department for three years each. He led the university's Faculty Consultative Committee in 2011–2012.<ref name=Insight2018/> From 2013 to 2018, he was associate dean for academic affairs in the U of M's [[University of Minnesota College of Science and Engineering|College of Sciences and Engineering]].<ref name=HigherEd2018/> He moved into the position of associate dean for research and planning in 2018, then became vice president for research later that year on the retirement of predecessor [[Allen Levine]]. Cramer oversaw one of the largest public-research programs in the United States,<ref name=MNDaily20181106>{{cite news |last=Macalus |first=Austen |date=2018-11-06 |title=New VP of research looks to future of research funding |url=http://www.mndaily.com/article/2018/11/n-new-vp-of-research-looks-to-future-of-research-funding |work=[[Minnesota Daily]] |location=[[Minneapolis, Minnesota]] |access-date=2020-09-01 |archive-date=2018-11-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106163849/http://www.mndaily.com/article/2018/11/n-new-vp-of-research-looks-to-future-of-research-funding |url-status=dead }}</ref> managing the administration, planning, and regulation of nearly $1 billion in research projects across the entire University of Minnesota system, including economic and technical development, and interdisciplinary efforts involving transportation and the environment.<ref name=Insight2018/><ref name=MNDaily20181010>{{cite news |last=Griffith |first=Michelle |date=2018-10-10 |title=Kaler appoints new vice president for research |url=https://www.mndaily.com/article/2018/10/n-umn-appoints-new-vice-president-of-university-research |work=[[Minnesota Daily]] |location=[[Minneapolis, Minnesota]] |access-date=2020-09-01 |archive-date=2020-03-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200331135902/https://www.mndaily.com/article/2018/10/n-umn-appoints-new-vice-president-of-university-research |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2021, he left the University of Minnesota and became the senior vice president and chief research officer for [[UL (safety organization)|Underwriters Laboratories Inc]].<ref name="APNewswire2021" /> He made this career move shortly after his wife, [[Laura Gagliardi]], left the University of Minnesota for a faculty position at the [[University of Chicago]]. 

Cramer was editor-in-chief (and before that, associate editor) of the scientific journal ''[[Theoretical Chemistry Accounts]]'' from 1997 to 2014. He was associate editor for the ''[[Journal of Physical Organic Chemistry]]'' from 1997 to 2018.<ref name=Insight2018/><ref name=UofMCramer/>

He is the author of the 2013 textbook ''Essentials of Computational Chemistry: Theories and Models''.<ref name="Cramer2013"/> Cramer also helped pioneer the university's [[e-learning]] programs by developing the online course ''Statistical Molecular Thermodynamics''.<ref name=UofMChemNews2013a>{{cite web |url= http://www1.chem.umn.edu/news/news.lasso?serial=515 |title= Cramer receives Taylor Award of Distinguished Service |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2013-04-02 |website=Department of Chemistry News |publisher=[[University of Minnesota]] |access-date=2020-09-01}}</ref><ref name=Coursera_StatMolTherm/>

His research work has covered a wide area, including advancements in [[solar energy]] (as head of the Center for the Study of Charge Transfer and Charge Transport in Photoactivated Systems),<ref name=SciEnt2012>{{cite web |url= https://sciencebusiness.technewslit.com/?p=10967 |title=Energy Dept to Fund Minnesota Chemistry Computation Centers |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=August 23, 2012 |website=Science and Enterprise |access-date=2020-09-10}}</ref> and [[Computer simulation|computer simulations]] of [[Chemical weapon|chemical weapons]] to assist in identification and cleanup.<ref name=MNDaily2011>{{cite news |last= Hargarten |first= Jeff |date=2011-12-12 |title=Department of Defense projects bring military touch to civilian research |url=http://www.mndaily.com/2011/12/12/department-defense-projects-bring-military-touch-civilian-research |work=[[Minnesota Daily]] |location=[[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]] |access-date=2020-09-01 }}</ref> He has also worked extensively with the [[Minnesota Supercomputing Institute]].<ref name=UofMChemNews2013a/>

Cramer has received several awards for teaching and public service. He was named a Distinguished McKnight University Professor,<ref name=McKnight>{{cite web |url= https://scholarswalk.umn.edu/faculty-awards/mcknight-awards/distinguished |title=Distinguished McKnight University Professors |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=University of Minnesota |access-date=2020-09-10}}</ref> received the George W. Taylor Award of Distinguished Service in 2013,<ref name=UofMChemNews2013a/> and the Horace T. Morse-University of Minnesota Alumni Association Award for Outstanding Contributions to Undergraduate Education in 2011.<ref name=UofMChemNews2011b>{{cite web |url= http://www1.chem.umn.edu/news/news.lasso?serial=133 |title= Professor Cramer receives Morse Alumni Award |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2011-03-30 |website=Department of Chemistry News |publisher=[[University of Minnesota]] |access-date=2020-09-01}}</ref>

He has also worked to increase public awareness and appreciation of science, and has been quoted in news articles and television reports as an expert on popular chemistry-related topics such as [[tear gas]] and [[pepper spray]],<ref name=Philly2020>{{cite news |last=Stacey |first= Burling |date=2020-06-03 |title=Tear gas has been controlling crowds for a century. How does it work? Can it cause permanent harm? |url=https://www.inquirer.com/news/what-is-tear-gas-demonstrations-coronavirus-philadelphia-washington-20200602.html |work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]] |location=[[Philadelphia]] |access-date=2020-09-10 }}</ref><ref name=WUSA2020>{{cite news |last=Block |first=Eliana |date=2020-06-20 |title=VERIFY: No, baking soda and water will not stop burning sensation from pepper spray |url=https://www.wusa9.com/article/news/verify/verify-baking-soda-and-water-mixture-will-not-stop-pepper-spray-burn/65-57595815-d833-489a-99da-9e3b060e4a33 |work=[[WUSA (TV)]] |location=[[Washington, D.C.]] |access-date=2020-09-10 }}</ref> [[Gunge|slime]],<ref name=Fox9Slime>{{cite news |date=March 9, 2017 |title='Slime' is the latest hot toy, but how safe is it? |url=https://www.fox9.com/news/slime-is-the-latest-hot-toy-but-how-safe-is-it |work=FOX 9 |location=[[Minneapolis-St. Paul]] |access-date=2020-09-10 }}</ref> [[Sodium chloride|road salt]],<ref name=WCCO2013>{{cite news |last=Brown |first=Heather |date=December 4, 2013 |title=Good Question: How Does Salt Melt Ice? |url=https://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2013/12/04/good-question-how-does-salt-melt-ice/ |work=[[WCCO-TV]] |location=[[Minneapolis-St. Paul]] |access-date=2020-09-10 }}</ref> and the persistence of particular smells.<ref name="livescience_65664">{{cite news |last= Weisberger |first= Mindy |date= June 9, 2019 |title=Why Are Some Smells So Hard to Get Rid Of? |url=https://www.livescience.com/65664-why-smells-linger.html |work=[[Live Science]] |access-date=2020-09-10 }}</ref>

==Publications==
Even after moving into administrative roles, Cramer continued to be active in scientific research. Cramer has written or co-written more than 500 articles for scientific journals and other scholarly publications.<ref name=CramerGroupPublications>{{cite web |url= http://pollux.chem.umn.edu/publications.html |title=Publications |website=The Cramer Group|publisher=[[University of Minnesota]] |access-date=2020-09-10}}</ref><ref name=Insight2018/> He has also written or edited several books, as follows:

===As author===
*''Essentials of Computational Chemistry: Theories and Models'' (2013)<ref name="Cramer2013">{{cite book|author=Christopher J. Cramer|title=Essentials of Computational Chemistry: Theories and Models|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=k4R6cf7I7q0C|date=29 April 2013|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-1-118-71227-6}}</ref>
*''Statistical Molecular Thermodynamics'' (Coursera Massive Open Online Course)<ref name=Coursera_StatMolTherm>{{cite web |url= https://www.coursera.org/learn/statistical-thermodynamics |title=Statistical Molecular Thermodynamics |last=Cramer |first=Christopher J. |website=Coursera |access-date=2020-09-10}}</ref><ref name=KAUST2018>{{cite web |url=https://kcc.kaust.edu.sa/2018-KAUST-Research-Conference/Pages/Speaker.aspx?si=1 |title=Speakers: Professor & Associate Dean Christopher J. Cramer |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2018 |website=KAUST Research Conference: New Challenges in Heterogeneous Catalysis |publisher=[[King Abdullah University of Science and Technology]] |access-date=2020-09-01 }}{{Dead link|date=December 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===As editor===
*''Structure and Reactivity in Aqueous Solution: Characterization of Chemical and Biological Systems'' (American Chemical Society Symposium Series, 1994)<ref name="CramerTruhlar1994">{{cite book|editor=Christopher J. Cramer, Donald G. Truhlar|title=Structure and Reactivity in Aqueous Solution: Characterization of Chemical and Biological Systems|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YRrwAAAAMAAJ|series=American Chemical Society Symposium Series|volume=568|year=1994|publisher=American Chemical Society|isbn=978-0-8412-2980-8}}</ref>
*''Theoretical Chemistry Accounts: New Century Issue'' (2000; a special reprint of Vol. 103, issues 3-4 of the journal)<ref name="CramerTruhlar2000">{{cite book|editor=Christopher Cramer, D.G. Truhlar|title=Theoretical Chemistry Accounts: New Century Issue|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jz_zCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA164|year=2000|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-662-10421-7}}</ref>
*''Perspectives on Theoretical Chemistry: Five Decades of Theoretical Chemistry Accounts and Theoretica Chimica Acta''<ref name="CramerTruhlar2012">{{cite book|editor=Christopher Cramer, D.G. Truhlar|title=Perspectives on Theoretical Chemistry: Five Decades of Theoretical Chemistry Accounts and Theoretica Chimica Acta|url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783642284441|year=2012|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-642-28444-1}}</ref>

==Awards and fellowships==
*In 2010, he was named a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name=ACSFellows>{{cite web |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/fellows.html |title=ACS Fellows Program |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= American Chemical Society |access-date=2020-09-10}}</ref> In August 2020, he received the society's Arthur C. Cope Scholar award for 2021.<ref name=ACSCopeScholar2021>{{cite magazine |url=https://cen.acs.org/people/awards/ACS-2021-national-award-winners/98/i31 |title=ACS 2021 national award winners|last=Wang|first=Linda|date=August 13, 2020 | magazine =Chemical and Engineering News|volume=98|issue=31 |publisher=American Chemical Society |access-date=2020-09-10}}</ref> 
* In 2000, he was named a Fellow of the [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]].<ref name=GuggenheimFellow>{{cite web |url= https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/christopher-j-cramer/ |title=All Fellows: Christopher J. Cramer |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation |access-date=2020-09-10}}</ref>
* In 1996, he was named a Fellow of the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]].<ref name=SloanFellow>{{cite web |url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows |title=Past Fellows |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |access-date=2020-09-10 |archive-date=2018-03-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314000756/https://sloan.org/past-fellows |url-status=dead }}</ref> 
* In 1991, he received the [[Arthur S Flemming Award]].<ref name=FlemmingAward>{{cite web |url=https://tspppa.gwu.edu/arthur-s-flemming-awards |title=Flemming Awardees |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= Arthur S Flemming Awards |access-date=2021-05-30}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Cramer is married to [[University of Chicago]] chemistry professor [[Laura Gagliardi]]; the couple has three children from a prior marriage.<ref name=Insight2018/>
